# Chess: the REXX functions and ADDRESS CHESS

<!-- Generated by tools/gen-commands.mjs from app/chess/described.ts (LISTCOMMANDS(1)) and app/chess/script.ts: edit those, then
     run `node --no-warnings tools/gen-commands.mjs`. run-tests.sh's `commands-doc` entry fails when this file differs. -->

Every action on the game is a command (`app/chess/commands.ts`), and each has a REXX function (`app/chess/control.ts`).
A script in the app, any REXX program on the machine (over sae's control bus) and an AI client (through the MCP server)
all call the same functions. The old app's `ADDRESS CHESS` lines (`move from=e2 to=e4`) work as they did.

## Quick start

```rexx
/* In the app, or from outside: REQUIRE "./chess-address.js" first (rexx/README.md) */
ADDRESS CHESS
'MOVE("e2", "e4")'            /* RESULT is the move in SAN: e4 */
"move from=c7 to=c5"           /* an old line, as before */
'GETBOARD()'
SAY RESULT
```

In a script inside the app the functions are called directly too: `r = MOVESAN("Nf3")`, `SAY GETFEN()`.

## The functions

48 of them, as `LISTCOMMANDS(1)` gives them. Optional parameters are in brackets. A function that cannot do what it is asked
(an illegal move, a square that is none, a FEN that is wrong) fails with the reason, which a script sees as its error and
the bus and the MCP server give back.

| Function | Does | Gives |
|---|---|---|
| [`CHESS_VERSION()`](#chess_version) | The app's version | e.g. "sae chess" |
| [`MOVE(from, to, [promotion])`](#move) | Makes a move, from a square to a square, for the side to move | the move in SAN, e.g. "Nf3" or "e8=Q+" |
| [`MOVESAN(move)`](#movesan) | Makes a move named in algebraic notation | the move in SAN |
| [`UNDO()`](#undo) | Takes back the last move (or the moves one request made, as one) | how many moves came back, 0 for none |
| [`REDO()`](#redo) | Makes again the last move taken back | how many moves went back on, 0 for none |
| [`NEWGAME()`](#newgame) | Starts a new game from the usual position; the settings stay | "OK" |
| [`SETPOSITION(fen)`](#setposition) | Sets up a position; the game starts from it | the position's FEN, as the app writes it |
| [`RESIGN([side])`](#resign) | Resigns; the game is over | the result, "1-0" or "0-1" |
| [`OFFERDRAW()`](#offerdraw) | Offers a draw, which is agreed (no one declines yet); the game is over | "1/2-1/2" |
| [`GETBOARD()`](#getboard) | The board as a diagram, white at the bottom: the Unicode pieces, "." for an empty square | ten lines of text |
| [`GETFEN()`](#getfen) | The position | its FEN |
| [`GETMOVES()`](#getmoves) | The legal moves for the side to move, in coordinate notation | a stem of "e2e4", "e7e8q", ... |
| [`LISTLEGALMOVES()`](#listlegalmoves) | The legal moves for the side to move, each described | a stem of {from, to, piece, capture, promotion, san, coordinate} |
| [`GETSTATUS()`](#getstatus) | Where the game is | {status, toPlay, isCheck, legalMoves, result}: status in_progress, check, checkmate, stalemate, fifty_move_draw, threefold_repetition_draw, insufficient_material_draw, resigned or draw_agreed |
| [`GETMOVEHISTORY()`](#getmovehistory) | The moves made so far, in coordinate notation | a stem of "e2e4", "e7e5", ... |
| [`GETMOVEHISTORYSAN()`](#getmovehistorysan) | The moves made so far, in SAN | a stem of "e4", "e5", ... |
| [`GETGAMEINFO()`](#getgameinfo) | Everything about the game at once | {status, toPlay, isCheck, legalMoveCount, halfMoveClock, fullMoveNumber, result, fen, lastMove, moves, canUndo, canRedo, aiLevel, aiSide, flipped, board} |
| [`GOTOMOVE(ply)`](#gotomove) | Goes to a move of the game, by undo or redo (a request's moves stay together); the moves after it can be redone | how many moves are made now |
| [`GETCAPTURED()`](#getcaptured) | The pieces taken since the start position, and the material balance (pawn 1, knight and bishop 3, rook 5, queen 9) | {white: the FEN letters of the black pieces white has taken, black: the white pieces black has taken, balance: above 0 when white is ahead} |
| [`GAMESCRIPT()`](#gamescript) | The game as a REXX program that plays it again: NEWGAME() (or SETPOSITION of where it started), then a MOVE line a move | the program's text, a line a move |
| [`EXPORTGAME()`](#exportgame) | The game as its file (what Save writes): where it started, its moves, who the computer plays, its level, the flip | the file's JSON: {format: "sae-chess-game", version: 1, start, moves, aiLevel, aiSide, flipped} |
| [`IMPORTGAME(file)`](#importgame) | Opens a game from its file's JSON, in place of this one (what Open reads) | how many moves it has |
| [`EXPORTPGN()`](#exportpgn) | The game in PGN: the seven tag roster (and the tags of a game read from PGN), SetUp and FEN when it did not start from the usual position, the moves in SAN, the result; comments and variations a PGN read had come back after their moves | the PGN text |
| [`IMPORTPGN(pgn)`](#importpgn) | Reads a game from PGN in place of this one: its moves played, its result (a resignation or agreed draw when the moves do not reach it); comments, variations and annotations kept for EXPORTPGN | how many moves it has |
| [`SAVEGAME(name)`](#savegame) | Keeps the game in the app, by a name, as its file (the moves, who the computer plays, its level, the flip): no file to pick | the name |
| [`OPENGAME(name)`](#opengame) | Opens a game kept by SAVEGAME, in place of this one | how many moves it has |
| [`LISTGAMES()`](#listgames) | The games kept in the app (SAVEGAME) | a stem of their names, in order |
| [`FORGETGAME(name)`](#forgetgame) | Forgets a game kept by SAVEGAME | the name |
| [`GETTURN()`](#getturn) | Whose move it is | "white" or "black" |
| [`GETRESULT()`](#getresult) | The result | "1-0", "0-1", "1/2-1/2", or "*" while the game goes on |
| [`PIECEAT(square)`](#pieceat) | What stands on a square | its FEN letter: K Q R B N P for white, k q r b n p for black, "" for none |
| [`ISCHECK()`](#ischeck) | Whether the side to move is in check | 1 or 0 |
| [`SETAIDIFFICULTY(level)`](#setaidifficulty) | Sets the computer player's level: how many half-moves it looks ahead (then the captures that follow) | the level |
| [`GETAIDIFFICULTY()`](#getaidifficulty) | The computer player's level | 1 to 4 |
| [`SETAISIDE(side)`](#setaiside) | Which side the computer plays | the side |
| [`AIMOVE()`](#aimove) | The computer makes a move for the side to move, at its level (SETAIDIFFICULTY): one step of undo; the same position at the same level gives the same move. It thinks in slices, so a level-4 move inside one control-bus request is not stopped at sae's limit for one piece of work | the move in SAN |
| [`ANALYZE([depth])`](#analyze) | What the computer makes of the position: its value, the best move and the line it expects (the game is not changed) | {value: to white in centipawns, above 0 when white is better; mate: moves to a mate found, above 0 when white mates, below when black does, 0 for none; text: "+0.35" or "#2"; best: the best move in SAN; coordinate: it as "e2e4"; pv: a stem of the line in SAN; depth; nodes} |
| [`HINT()`](#hint) | The move the computer would play for the side to move, at its level (the game is not changed) | the move in SAN |
| [`OPENINGNAME()`](#openingname) | The name of the opening the game is in: the last position of the opening book (written for this app from the openings' public names) the game passed through, transpositions too | e.g. "Ruy Lopez, Morphy Defence"; "" before the first named position, or for a game set up from another |
| [`BOOKMOVES()`](#bookmoves) | The opening book's moves from the position now | a stem of moves in SAN; none once the game is out of the book |
| [`SETBOOK([on])`](#setbook) | Whether the computer plays from the opening book while the game is in it (AIMOVE then makes a book move at once, chosen by the position) | 1 when on, else 0 |

### CHESS_VERSION

```rexx
CHESS_VERSION()
```

The app's version. Gives e.g. "sae chess".

### MOVE

```rexx
MOVE(from, to, [promotion])
```

Makes a move, from a square to a square, for the side to move. Gives the move in SAN, e.g. "Nf3" or "e8=Q+".

| Parameter | Kind | |
|---|---|---|
| `from` | square |  |
| `to` | square |  |
| `promotion` | piece, optional | queen if left out, when the move promotes |

### MOVESAN

```rexx
MOVESAN(move)
```

Makes a move named in algebraic notation. Gives the move in SAN.

| Parameter | Kind | |
|---|---|---|
| `move` | san | or coordinate notation, "e2e4", "e7e8q" |

### UNDO

```rexx
UNDO()
```

Takes back the last move (or the moves one request made, as one). Gives how many moves came back, 0 for none.

### REDO

```rexx
REDO()
```

Makes again the last move taken back. Gives how many moves went back on, 0 for none.

### NEWGAME

```rexx
NEWGAME()
```

Starts a new game from the usual position; the settings stay. Gives "OK".


Goes to a move of the game, by undo or redo (a request's moves stay together); the moves after it can be redone. Gives how many moves are made now.

|---|---|---|
| `ply` | number | how many moves in: 0 for the start, 1 after white's first, 2 after black's, ... |

### AIMOVE

```rexx
AIMOVE()
```

The computer makes a move for the side to move, at its level (SETAIDIFFICULTY): one step of undo; the same position at the same level gives the same move. It thinks in slices, so a level-4 move inside one control-bus request is not stopped at sae's limit for one piece of work. Gives the move in SAN.

### ANALYZE

```rexx
ANALYZE([depth])
```

What the computer makes of the position: its value, the best move and the line it expects (the game is not changed). Gives {value: to white in centipawns, above 0 when white is better; mate: moves to a mate found, above 0 when white mates, below when black does, 0 for none; text: "+0.35" or "#2"; best: the best move in SAN; coordinate: it as "e2e4"; pv: a stem of the line in SAN; depth; nodes}.

| Parameter | Kind | |
|---|---|---|
| `depth` | level, optional | how many half-moves to look: 1 to 4; the computer's level if left out |

### HINT

```rexx
HINT()
```

The move the computer would play for the side to move, at its level (the game is not changed). Gives the move in SAN.

### OPENINGNAME

```rexx
OPENINGNAME()
```

The name of the opening the game is in: the last position of the opening book (written for this app from the openings' public names) the game passed through, transpositions too. Gives e.g. "Ruy Lopez, Morphy Defence"; "" before the first named position, or for a game set up from another.

### BOOKMOVES

```rexx
BOOKMOVES()
```

The opening book's moves from the position now. Gives a stem of moves in SAN; none once the game is out of the book.

### SETBOOK

```rexx
SETBOOK([on])
```

Whether the computer plays from the opening book while the game is in it (AIMOVE then makes a book move at once, chosen by the position). Gives 1 when on, else 0.

| Parameter | Kind | |
|---|---|---|
| `on` | flag, optional | 1: on, 0: off; left out: the other one |

### FLIPBOARD

```rexx
FLIPBOARD()
```

Turns the board round: black at the bottom, or white again. Gives 1 when black is at the bottom, else 0.

### BOARDSIZE

```rexx
BOARDSIZE([px])
```

Sets the board's size on the page, in pixels; by itself the board follows the window, the largest square there is room for. Gives the size, in pixels.

| Parameter | Kind | |
|---|---|---|
| `px` | number, optional | 240 to 960, which the board then keeps; "fit": it follows the window again; left out: the size it is |

### DARKMODE

```rexx
DARKMODE([on])
```

The page's dark look, or the light. Gives 1 when dark, else 0.

| Parameter | Kind | |
|---|---|---|
| `on` | flag, optional | 1: dark, 0: light; left out: the other one |

### CHESSCOMMAND

```rexx
CHESSCOMMAND(line)
```

Runs one ADDRESS CHESS line, as a script's ADDRESS CHESS does (the control bus, whose requests are expressions, reaches the old commands so). Gives what the line gives; its refusal is the error.

| Parameter | Kind | |
|---|---|---|
| `line` | text | an ADDRESS CHESS line: "move from=e2 to=e4", "get-board", or a command such as "game.move san=Nf3" |

### RUN_PROGRAM

```rexx
RUN_PROGRAM(program, [encoding])
```

Runs a whole program with these same functions, as one step of undo, taken back whole if it fails. Gives {said: a stem of its SAY lines, result: its RESULT}.

| Parameter | Kind | |
|---|---|---|
| `program` | text | a whole REXX program: lines, loops, routines |
| `encoding` | text, optional | "json": the program is a JSON string |

### LISTCOMMANDS

```rexx
LISTCOMMANDS([described])
```

The functions a script may call. Gives a stem of names, or of {name, signature, params, does, gives}.

| Parameter | Kind | |
|---|---|---|
| `described` | flag, optional | 1: each with its parameters, what it does and what it gives |

### BATCH_EXECUTE

```rexx
BATCH_EXECUTE(commands, [stop])
```

Runs each command in turn, by name. Gives a JSON array of {index, command, success, result or error}.

| Parameter | Kind | |
|---|---|---|
| `commands` | stem | of {command, args}; or their JSON |
| `stop` | flag, optional | 1: the first that fails is the call's error (a control-bus request is then taken back whole) |

## The kinds of parameter

| Kind | What it is |
|---|---|
| square | a square, `"e4"` |
| san | a move in standard algebraic notation, `"Nf3"`, `"O-O"`, `"exd5"`, `"e8=Q"` (coordinate notation, `"e2e4"`, too) |
| fen | a position in FEN |
| piece | a promotion piece: queen, rook, bishop or knight (or q, r, b, n) |
| side | white or black (for the computer player: white, black, both or none) |
| level | the computer player's level, 1 to 4 |
| text, number, flag, json, stem | text; a number; 1 or 0; JSON as text; a REXX stem (`list.0` how many, `list.1`, ...) |

## The old ADDRESS CHESS lines

The old app's twelve commands, each now a function. A line's RESULT is what the function gives, as JSON text where the old
gave JSON. A line of the app's own commands works too: `ADDRESS CHESS "game.move san=Nf3"`.

| Line | Is now |
|---|---|
| `move from=e2 to=e4` | `MOVE()` |
| `get-board` | `GETBOARD()` |
| `get-moves` | `GETMOVES()`, as JSON |
| `list-legal-moves` | `LISTLEGALMOVES()`, as JSON |
| `undo` | `UNDO()` |
| `redo` | `REDO()` |
| `new-game` | `NEWGAME()` |
| `set-ai-difficulty level=3` | `SETAIDIFFICULTY()` |
| `get-status` | `GETSTATUS()`, as JSON |
| `get-move-history` | `GETMOVEHISTORY()`, as JSON |
| `get-position-fen` | `GETFEN()` |
| `get-game-info` | `GETGAMEINFO()`, as JSON |

### RC, RESULT and ERRORTEXT

In a script in the app: RC is 0 when the line worked, 1 when it was refused (ERRORTEXT and RESULT say why), and 2 for a
command there is none of. The old app numbered its refusals (10-19 for `move`, 21-29 for `get-board`, ... 121-129 for
`get-game-info`); they are 1 now, each with its reason. From another program over the bus (`rexx/chess-address.js`),
RC is 1 for any refusal and 2 when there is no app to ask.

```rexx
ADDRESS CHESS "move from=e2 to=e5"
IF RC <> 0 THEN SAY "refused:" ERRORTEXT     /* e2 to e5 is not a legal move for white */
```

## Undo

`UNDO()` takes back a step: one move made on its own, or every move one script, one control-bus request or one MCP call
made, together. `REDO()` makes a step again. A request or a call that fails part way is taken back whole, and its error
ends "(nothing it did was kept)".

## From another program: the control bus

Started with `--control-bus` (`../sae/target/build/bin/sae --app app --control-bus`), the app answers requests from this
machine on sae's sealed control bus (sae's `docs/control-bus.md`). A request is one REXX expression, worked out as
`LET RESULT = <request>`:

```bash
../sae/target/sae-bus Chess 'MOVE("e2", "e4")'
../sae/target/sae-bus Chess 'MOVESAN("e5"); MOVESAN("Nf3")'     # one step of undo
../sae/target/sae-bus Chess 'CHESSCOMMAND("get-status")'         # an old line
```

From REXX, `REQUIRE "./chess-address.js"` and `ADDRESS CHESS` ([rexx/README.md](rexx/README.md)). sae stops a request
whose work runs past 5 s at a stretch, and answers for one still running at 10 s; the app takes either back whole.

## From an AI client: the MCP server

`mcp/chess-mcp.js` ([mcp/README.md](mcp/README.md)) offers `chess_move`, `chess_board`, `chess_call` (any function above
by name, its arguments checked against `LISTCOMMANDS(1)` before anything is sent), `chess_run_program` (a whole REXX
program, one step of undo) and `chess_list_commands`; `--tools=rexx` or `all` add `chess_run`, one REXX command.

```bash
claude mcp add chess -- node /path/to/chaess/mcp/chess-mcp.js
```

## Examples

`rexx/reference-examples.rexx`, as it is; `spec_app_chess_rexx` runs it against the app. Inside the app, drop the
`REQUIRE` line.

```rexx
-- reference-examples.rexx: CHESS_COMMANDS.md's examples, included there as
-- they are by tools/gen-commands.mjs, and run against the app by
-- spec_app_chess_rexx. From the repository's root, with the app running
-- (--control-bus): RexxJS/core/rexx rexx/reference-examples.rexx
REQUIRE "./chess-address.js"
ADDRESS CHESS "new-game"

/* An opening, by the old lines */
ADDRESS CHESS "move from=e2 to=e4"
ADDRESS CHESS "move from=c7 to=c5"
ADDRESS CHESS "move from=g1 to=f3"
ADDRESS CHESS "get-status"
SAY "Status: " RESULT

/* A move tried, and refused */
ADDRESS CHESS "move from=e7 to=e4"
IF RC = 0 THEN
  SAY "legal"
ELSE
  SAY "illegal:" ERRORTEXT

/* The functions: undo and redo, the position */
ADDRESS CHESS 'UNDO()'
SAY RESULT "move back"
ADDRESS CHESS 'REDO()'
ADDRESS CHESS 'GETFEN()'
SAY "FEN:" RESULT
```
